# Frozen canonical-CBOR conformance corpus, EXTRACTED from evermesh's conformance
# suite (tools/conformance/vectors, 189 vectors, spec 001 §2/§11) at evermesh
# revision fd1694f4a8ea585f65cc01ebe40c74737b10a263 (2026-07-30).
#
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. kotva-cbor's encoder was seeded from evermesh-kernel's
# `codec` module, whose docs state cross-implementation byte identity as
# CONSENSUS-CRITICAL. This corpus is what keeps that claim testable inside kotva
# without kotva depending on evermesh: every `accept` line's bytes MUST decode and
# then re-encode to exactly themselves (the malleability guarantee), and every
# `reject` line MUST be refused.
#
# It is a SNAPSHOT, not a live mirror. Regenerate deliberately, and record in the
# commit which evermesh revision it was taken from; a corpus that silently tracks
# upstream would hide the divergence it exists to catch.
#
# FORMAT: one vector per line, `<verdict> <group>/<name> <lowercase hex>`.
#   accept  canonical CBOR: decode_canonical MUST succeed and re-encode identically.
#           (Some of these are `record-invalid` vectors whose defect is at the
#           envelope/signature/kind layer, ABOVE the codec — the bytes themselves
#           are perfectly canonical, so the codec must accept them.)
#   reject  evermesh classifies the defect as `cbor` or `non-canonical`:
#           decode_canonical MUST refuse.
#
# NOTE: `json/negative-integer-key` encodes `{-3: null}`. It is canonical CBOR and
# kotva-cbor accepts it; kotva-core's narrower `Cv` does not (no Nint, no Null).
# That asymmetry is deliberate and is asserted in kotva-core's own tests.
#
# vectors: 183 (153 accept, 30 reject)
#
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# SECOND-ORDER COPY NOTICE (magnetite-seams).
#
# This file is byte-for-byte identical to kotva's copy at
# `crates/kotva-cbor/tests/vectors/evermesh-canonical-cbor.txt`, taken from
# kotva revision b5bf8cf2e594eeeedfe0045c591a6c00f094624f (2026-07-30). It did
# NOT come from evermesh directly — magnetite-seams has no dependency on
# either kotva or evermesh (product standalone-ness rule), so this is a copy
# of a copy, and the chain is recorded here rather than assumed.
#
# WHY THIS COPY EXISTS. `magnetite_seams::cbor` is a third, hand-written,
# independent implementation of the same canonical-CBOR encoding described
# above. It had never been checked against this corpus before. Its `Cv` type
# is strictly narrower than kotva's `Value` — no negative integers, no `null`,
# and map keys are `u64` only (no text, bool, array or map keys) — so most of
# this corpus's `accept` vectors, which exercise evermesh's text-keyed
# per-kind record bodies, do NOT apply to `Cv` at all: `Cv` cannot represent
# the value that's supposed to be accepted, structurally, not because the
# codec is wrong. `magnetite-seams/tests/evermesh_conformance.rs` computes the
# applicable shared subset from the decoded shape of each vector (not a
# hand-maintained label list) and asserts its size, so a corpus edit that
# changes the subset fails the test until the expected counts are updated
# alongside it. Every `reject` vector applies unconditionally: refusal is not
# type-specific, so `Cv`'s narrower domain can only refuse a superset of what
# `kotva_cbor::Value` refuses.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
